title: Sigil configuration file
description: The configuration of a Sigil policy repository: sigil.yaml, sigil.json or sigil.toml, or the same with a leading dot. Paths are relative to the file's directory. See https://sigil.specht-labs.de/reference/config/.

$schema.description: The JSON Schema the file follows, for editors. The tools ignore it.

kinds.description: Kind files outside the paths a command reads, which every policy command loads as if named with --kind.

anyOf.description: A kind file, relative to the configuration file.

items.description: A kind file, relative to the configuration file.

lints.description: The level of each lint: off, warn or error. Lints the file doesn't name keep their defaults.

duplicate-invocation.description: A policy is invoked twice with the same arguments, in any order. Default warn.

gated-assert.description: A policy holding asserts, directly or through its own invocations, is invoked under `when` and isn't required. Default warn.

gated-deny.description: A policy holding constructors of the decision a `collect one` kind ranks highest is invoked under `when` and isn't required. Default warn.

path-matches-name.description: A document's name doesn't match its file's path. Default off.

qualified-imports.description: A selective import is used. Default off.

shadowed-kind-name.description: A document keeps a name the kind has since given to an input, host function, decision, enum or enum value. Default warn.

unused-import.description: A `use` binds a name nothing reads or invokes. Default warn.

unused-let.description: A private let is never read. Default warn.

require.description: The policies sigil check enforces, one entry each. A policy can be required once.

items.description: A policy every root it applies to must invoke unconditionally.

policy.description: The required policy's name: one name, not a pattern.

roots.description: Name patterns of the policies the requirement applies to, as --policy takes them. Without it, every policy of the required policy's kind that no other policy invokes.

anyOf.description: A policy name or pattern, such as "payments.*".

items.description: A policy name or pattern, such as "payments.*".

trusted.description: Files and directories the required policy comes from, as --trusted reads them.

anyOf.description: A file or directory, relative to the configuration file.

items.description: A file or directory, relative to the configuration file.

trusted.description: Files and directories read as trusted, as --trusted reads them: their documents resolve first, and no other document may take a name they define.

anyOf.description: A file or directory, relative to the configuration file.

items.description: A file or directory, relative to the configuration file.
